episode_title: Leading on Your Terms: Lessons from a CEO

real_qa.q: What is Symfolio and how does it streamline the furniture procurement process?
real_qa.r: Symfolio is the first SaaS-based platform for the commercial furniture industry designed for clients, dealers, and designers to get through the procurement process. The tool extracts information from end users with minimal questions—typically 8 to 10 questions cut out about 8 to 10 weeks in the design process—quickly aligning on budget and allowing clients to understand how and where they will spend their dollars across the floor plate.

real_qa.q: How did SKG move from being a vendor to becoming a strategic partner in commercial furniture?
real_qa.r: SKG transformed by getting deeply engaged into the business with clients—learning why they exist, understanding their culture, how employees work and want to work, and learning about their customers. The approach is to help clients align their strategic business goals to their real estate footprint, with the end product being furniture but the real work being business strategy and workplace strategy.
real_qa.requete: SKG commercial furniture strategic partner approach

real_qa.q: What drove Beth Goff McMillan to start her first consulting company as a single mother?
real_qa.r: She wanted to change the commercial furniture industry by shifting the conversation from design and products to focusing on the end user and solving for space. She also wanted to make her own schedule, work with people she believed in, choose customers she wanted to be associated with, and find more time to be a mother. She used her pool money to start the company, telling her children they could use the public pool while she invested in her entrepreneurial vision.
real_qa.requete: Beth Goff McMillan started consulting company single mother

real_qa.q: What statistic does Beth Goff McMillan cite about women and job application confidence?
real_qa.r: Most women won't apply for a job unless they have 85 to 90 percent of all the skill sets listed, whereas men will apply if they have 50 percent or less of the required skills. This gap in confidence and self-advocacy is a key barrier young women face when entering the job market.
real_qa.requete: women job applications 85 percent skill requirement

real_qa.q: How does Beth Goff McMillan define confidence in a professional context?
real_qa.r: Confidence is a repeatable act—a successful, repeatable act. It comes through finding balance between what you know and what you don't know, being willing to learn, staying curious, and proving yourself through consistent actions over time rather than having everything figured out on day one.

real_qa.q: Why did the furniture industry traditionally deprioritize furniture procurement in commercial real estate projects?
real_qa.r: In a typical two-year commercial real estate process, furniture is handled by the last rung on the ladder after the corporate real estate broker, project manager, architect, designer, and general contractor have their input. Furniture stakeholders are given less than three months to complete their work despite furniture being one of the largest expenditures—often millions of dollars—and the physical connection between people and their work.
real_qa.requete: commercial furniture procurement timeline three months

guest.bio_context: Beth Goff McMillan is the CEO of SKG, one of the largest women-owned businesses in Texas, and has spent the past 25 years in the commercial furnishings industry. She is the founder of Symfolio, a SaaS platform built from inside the industry to streamline furniture procurement. Born and raised in Louisville, Kentucky, she began her career as an intern at a furniture dealership while a sophomore in college, later worked for global manufacturer Noel, started a consulting company, and built SKG into a statewide dealership business.
